newsitem.title: USA: Maine Yankee nuke plant resumes normal output.
newsitem.headline: Maine Yankee nuke plant resumes normal output.

text.p: The Maine Yankee nuclear power plant resumed normal output level over the weekend after an unexpected trip off line last Wednesday during testing of its reactor protective system, Maine Yankee Atomic Power Co said. "We went back on the grid Saturday night, and we were back up to 90 percent power by seven p.m. (1900 EDT) Sunday," said company spokeswoman Maureen Brown on Tuesday.
A preliminary review showed the shutdown of Maine Yankee was caused by a dip in power supply in a circuit board used only during the monthly testing of the system.

The 910 megawatt generating station in Wiscasset, Maine, has been limited to 90 percent capacity while the Nuclear Regulatory Commission inspected the results of new safety tests on the emergency core cooling system. Tests conducted in the 1980s are the focus of fraud allegations.

Maine Yankee Atomic Power operates the nuclear facility in Wiscasset, Maine, and is owned by a consortium of New England utilities including Central Maine Power Co 38 percent; New England Electric System 20 percent; and Northeast Utilities 20 percent.
